newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS GIVE TOMJANOVICH FOUR MORE YEARS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS GIVE TOMJANOVICH FOUR MORE YEARS.

text.p: The Houston Rockets extended head coach Rudy Tomjanovich's contract on Friday through the 2000-01 season. Terms were not disclosed.
Tomjanovich just completed his 27th season with the Rockets and sixth as head coach.
He has a 281-159 regular-season record and is 48-33 in the playoffs, including NBA Championships in 1994 and 1995. The team rewarded Tomjanovich with a new five-year deal following the second title.

"Winning is what the Rockets aim for every year," said Rockets owner and president Leslie Alexander. "We're very fortunate in Houston that we have a team and a coach who can achieve the success that the Rockets want for our fans in this city.
"We are really looking forward to this season with very high hopes, notwithstanding Michael (Jordan). We can beat the Bulls," Alexander said.

Tomjanovich played 11 seasons with the Rockets, averaging 17.4 points and 8.1 rebounds in 768 career contests. He was an assistant coach and a scout for six years before becoming a full-time assistant in 1988. After Don Chaney was fired in 1992, the Rockets appointed Tomjanovich as his replacement.
After acquiring All-Star forward Charles Barkley in a trade with Phoenix last summer, Houston went 57-25 in 1996-97 before losing to Utah in the Western Conference finals.
